reasons: Lake identity gives case_name New York v. Belton, court U.S. Supreme Court, year 1981.
Lake citations give official cite 453 U.S. 454, parallel cites 101 S. Ct. 2860 and 69 L. Ed. 2d 768, and vendor-neutral cite 1981 U.S. LEXIS 13.
Opinion text says the encounter began when a trooper stopped a speeding car.
The legal issue is search incident to arrest, so Traffic Stops as Related (cross-doctrine) is not overclaimed.
residual_risks: The home taxonomy itself is not defined in the lake record, but the related/cross-doctrine placement is supported by the disclosed opinion facts.

reasons: The opinion states the question was the permissible scope of a search of an automobile passenger compartment incident to lawful custodial arrest of an occupant.
The opinion adopts a vehicle search-incident-to-arrest rule for the passenger compartment and containers, supporting placement on SIA Vehicles as key/refinement material.

defect.evidence_quote: Accordingly, we hold that when a policeman has made a lawful custodial arrest of the occupant of an automobile,<footnotemark>2</footnotemark> he may, as a contemporaneous incident of that arrest, search the passenger compartment of that automobile.<footnotemark>3</footnotemark>
defect.problem: The holding field is truncated after 'police may search the...' and omits the limiting terms that make the rule accurate: contemporaneous incident, passenger compartment, and containers within that compartment.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the truncated holding with: Defines the scope of a vehicle search incident to arrest: when police make a lawful custodial arrest of an automobile occupant, they may, as a contemporaneous incident of that arrest, search the passenger compartment and examine containers found there.

reasons: The core premise that Belton defines the scope of a vehicle search incident to arrest is supported by the opinion.
As written, the field is incomplete and could be read too broadly without the passenger-compartment limitation.
residual_risks: Treatment limits from Gant are outside Lens A except as already flagged in the page treatment section.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add the container rule and the passenger-compartment-only limitation; avoid a generic 'police may search the vehicle' phrasing.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside Lens A's attack charter.

residual_risks: Lens B should assess treatment/currency substance.
